findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level` without a nil check. A `topic_users` row is not guaranteed to exist for the current user and topic (e.g. the link is shared/forwarded and opened by a different logged-in user, the row was removed, or the user simply visits `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never interacted with). In those cases the request raises `NoMethodError` on nil and returns a 500 instead of a useful page. The action should create/fetch the record (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) or handle nil gracefully.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET with no CSRF protection
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action mutates the user's `topic_users.notification_level` and is wired to GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`, `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) with `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`. Rails does not CSRF-protect GET requests, so any third-party page can silently change a logged-in user's notification level for an arbitrary topic with ``, and repeated loads will escalate the level to `muted` (see the toggle logic). Browser prefetching/link scanners and a plain page refresh have the same effect. Side effects should be performed behind a POST/PUT (or a signed unsubscribe key, like `email/unsubscribe/:key`) rather than a plain GET.

findings.title: Writing notification_level directly bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: The action assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` are never set, and no MessageBus `/topic/<id>` `notification_level_change` message is published. Two concrete consequences: (1) other open tabs/clients keep showing the stale notification level; (2) `TopicUser.update_last_read` only auto-bumps the level to `tracking` when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL`, so after this unsubscribe the next time the user reads the topic long enough their level is silently raised back to `tracking`, undoing the unsubscribe.

findings.title: Unsubscribe is not idempotent: reloading the page escalates to muted
findings.body: The logic is `if tu.notification_level > regular then regular else muted`. A watching/tracking user who opens the unsubscribe link gets `regular`; if the same URL is hit again (page refresh, back/forward navigation, browser or mail-client prefetch, or the user clicking the link in a second email) the level is now equal to `regular`, so the else branch sets `muted`. A single user action ("unsubscribe from this topic") can therefore silently escalate to full muting of the topic without any further confirmation. The endpoint should be idempotent, i.e. set a single deterministic target level.

findings.title: Unsubscribe page claims notifications will stop even when level is only lowered to 'regular'
findings.body: The page always renders `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` ("You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}."), but the server only sets the level to `regular` when the user was watching/tracking. At `regular` the user still receives notifications for replies to their posts, quotes and mentions in that topic, so the message is factually wrong for the most common case. The same applies to the new `unsubscribe_link` server string ("To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here"). The text should reflect the level that was actually applied.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} with no fallback
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` string gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder` adds no default for `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args`. Any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` (other mailers, forks, plugins) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in `MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part`, i.e. the email fails to send. The fact that `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` had to be changed to add `unsubscribe_url` confirms the hard dependency. Add a default (e.g. fall back to `user_preferences_url`) or only append the per-topic sentence when the option is present.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe endpoint or unsubscribe_url rendering
findings.body: The only test change is adding `unsubscribe_url` to an existing builder so the suite keeps passing. There is no spec asserting that the per-topic unsubscribe URL actually appears in the email body/HTML, no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, and no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. Given the nil-`TopicUser` crash, the non-idempotent toggle and the GET-based mutation, a controller spec covering (a) no existing topic_users row, (b) repeated requests, and (c) the slug redirect is needed to prevent regressions.

findings.title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` ("Notificiations") in both the controller and `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`. It works today because the typo is consistent, but it is a trap for future edits/overrides (a correctly spelled reference in a plugin or theme will silently render nothing). Rename to `stopNotificationsText` in both places.

findings.title: Class attribute contains a stray leading dot
findings.body: `<h4 class='.previous-discussion'>` sets the literal class name `.previous-discussion`, so any email stylesheet rule targeting `.previous-discussion` will never match. Since this line is being reformatted in this PR anyway, drop the leading dot.
